title: ICAB P2 - Audit and Assurance
summary: Covers acceptance, managing and performing audit and assurance engagements in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISAs), risk assessment, audit evidence, and auditor reporting.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Audit and Assurance. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Legal/Professional Regulations, Ethics & Acceptance
stages.name: Area 1: Legal/Professional Regulations, Ethics & Acceptance
stages.description: Statutory audit requirements, IESBA Code of Ethics, quality management (ISQM 1), and client acceptance.

nodes.name: ISQM 1, Professional Ethics & Client Acceptance
nodes.description: Appointment, removal, and duties of auditors under Companies Act 1994; FRC audit oversight; IESBA Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants; ISQM 1 Quality Management for Firms; client acceptance and engagement management.
topics: Auditor appointment, qualifications, disqualifications, and removal under Companies Act 1994
Role of Financial Reporting Council (FRC) Bangladesh in auditing oversight
IESBA Code fundamental principles, independence in mind and appearance
Ethical threats (long association, non-audit services, fee dependence) and safeguards
ISQM 1: System of quality management, governance, ethics, risk assessment, monitoring
Pre-conditions for audit (ISA 210), engagement letters, client onboarding and KYC
learningOutcomes: Evaluate compliance with Companies Act 1994 auditor appointment rules.
Design firm quality management procedures under ISQM 1.
Resolve complex independence and conflict of interest scenarios.
checklists: Practice 4 ethical threat scenarios with appropriate safeguards
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: Planning & Performing Audit Engagements
stages.name: Area 2: Planning & Performing Audit Engagements
stages.description: Audit risk (ISA 315), materiality (ISA 320), fraud (ISA 240), internal control evaluation, and substantive procedures.

nodes.name: Audit Risk Assessment & Materiality (ISA 315 & 320)
nodes.description: Audit risk model: Inherent risk, Control risk, Detection risk; understanding the entity and environment (ISA 315 Revised); planning and performance materiality (ISA 320); auditor responsibilities for fraud (ISA 240); IT environment risks and automated controls.
topics: The audit risk model: AR = IR x CR x DR and its practical application
ISA 315 (Revised 2019): Identifying and assessing risks of material misstatement (RMM)
Assessing IT general controls (ITGCs) and automated application controls
Determination of planning materiality, performance materiality, and trivial threshold (ISA 320)
Auditor's responsibilities relating to fraud in an audit (ISA 240): Fraud risk factors and skepticism
Laws and regulations in an audit (ISA 250): Direct vs indirect compliance
learningOutcomes: Calculate planning and performance materiality benchmarks.
Identify and assess risks of material misstatement at financial statement and assertion levels.
Design responses to address identified fraud risks.
checklists: Calculate materiality on 3 scenario financial statements
Draft risk and response audit planning matrix
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

nodes.name: Substantive Audit Procedures & Complex Balances
nodes.description: Designing substantive audit tests for complex areas: Revenue (IFRS 15), Inventory, Provisions, Going concern (ISA 570), Related parties (ISA 550), and Accounting estimates (ISA 540).
topics: Substantive testing methodology: Analytical procedures vs tests of details
Auditing revenue recognition under IFRS 15: Cut-off, rebates, multi-element contracts
Auditing inventory: Count attendance, valuation testing, NRV write-down testing
Auditing accounting estimates including fair value under ISA 540 (Revised)
Auditing related party transactions and disclosures under ISA 550
Going concern evaluation under ISA 570: Indicators, cash forecasts, and management support
Audit sampling techniques (ISA 530) and Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs)
learningOutcomes: Design detailed substantive audit programs for high-risk accounts.
Audit complex accounting estimates and fair value measurements.
Evaluate going concern adequacy and audit evidence.
checklists: Read Substantive Audit Procedures & Complex Balances in ICAB Study Manual
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Concluding & Reporting on Engagements
stages.name: Area 3: Concluding & Reporting on Engagements
stages.description: Subsequent events (ISA 560), written representations (ISA 580), and auditor reporting (ISA 700, 701, 705, 706).

nodes.name: Subsequent Events, Evaluation & Auditor's Report
nodes.description: Subsequent events up to and after report date (ISA 560); written representations from management (ISA 580); evaluating misstatements (ISA 450); Key Audit Matters (KAM - ISA 701); unmodified vs modified opinions (ISA 705); Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter paragraphs (ISA 706).
topics: Evaluating uncorrected misstatements against materiality thresholds (ISA 450)
Subsequent events procedures: Adjusting vs non-adjusting events under IAS 10 / ISA 560
Written representations: Purpose, limitations, and refusal to provide (ISA 580)
Standard unmodified auditor's report structure under ISA 700 (Revised)
Communicating Key Audit Matters (KAM) in listed entity reports (ISA 701)
Modifications to the opinion (ISA 705): Qualified, Adverse, Disclaimer of opinion
Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter paragraphs (ISA 706) criteria and placement
learningOutcomes: Determine required modifications to the audit opinion based on pervasive/material tests.
Draft Key Audit Matters (KAM) descriptions for listed entities.
Evaluate the impact of subsequent events on audit reports.
checklists: Memorize opinion decision matrix (Material vs Material & Pervasive)
Draft sample Key Audit Matter paragraph for inventory valuation
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
